** Finding 8 — (Round 2) The NaN/Inf trigger is per-variant: DIRECT_DILATION cannot emit NaN; three other variants can; the finite-check seam belongs at EvaluateCostFunction
- Structural audit (angle 02 R2): the oracle cost is white_sum_A + FastImplantDilationMetric + DistanceMapMetric; every intermediate is an int (ComputeSumWhitePixels int count; chamfer −1·int score; distance map int/(count+0.1) with a non-negative numerator and denominator ≥ 0.1). No float division, no sqrt, no asin, no uninitialized read; max accumulation 255·1024² ≈ 2.55e8 ≪ 2³¹. Verdict: DIRECT_DILATION returns a finite double for EVERY pose, including empty silhouettes, degenerate projections, and behind-camera poses. [Source: angles/02-cost-path-foundation.org, Round 2 "NaN/Inf emission audit"]
- The emitters, all production-reachable: (1) DIRECT_MAHFOUZ — `if (pixel_score_ != 0)` tests the pinned pointer, never the value (implant_mahfouz_metric.cu:324/446); with pixel_score_[0] == 0 the divisions give 0/0 NaN (selectable in production, forces dilation 3, optimizer_manager.cpp:252-253/270-271/288-289); (2) DD_NEW_POLE_CONSTRAINT — UB min_dist read can surface a NaN payload (compiler-dependent); (3) sym_trap — asin(fem2tib[2][1]) is NaN for |entry| > 1 (sym_trap_function.cpp:129), reachable through FP rounding. Int overflow and the DRR float-atomic path are ruled out. [Source: angles/02-cost-path-foundation.org, Round 2]
- Correction to the round-1/synthesis claim "NaN poisons hull slope comparisons": the data storage sorts each size-column descending (true minimum at the back); ConvexHull reads only the back. A NaN box fails every comparison and is inserted at the column FRONT — never selected, never popped (pops the back), never read by the hull. Actual NaN behavior: (a) `result < current_optimum_value_` is false, so a NaN eval never updates the optimum; (b) the NaN box accumulates as dead weight (lost evals, unbounded growth); (c) the column minimum becomes NaN only after all finite boxes in that column are trisected away — delayed, conditional poisoning. The finite-check is motivated by (a)+(b), not the round-1 claim. [Source: angles/02-cost-path-foundation.org, Round 2; src/domain/direct_data_storage.cpp:92-131]
- The finite-check wraps DirectOptimizer::EvaluateCostFunction (direct_optimizer.cpp:205) — the single chokepoint shared by production (RunDirectStage), the oracle, and the coordinator; CUDA-free (headless-testable), one std::isfinite per eval. Design: `if (!std::isfinite(result)) { non_finite_count_++; /* GLh: result = f_min + d(x,x_min) when enabled; else treat as infeasible (do not store, never wins the optimum) */ }` plus GetNonFiniteCount() and an iteration-callback event. The GPU side needs NO checks — all GPU outputs are provably finite ints. Probes: Tier-0 headless (fake cost lambda returning NaN/±Inf/sNaN; asserts no crash, counter increments, optimum never reflects a non-finite eval, GLh surrogate behavior, surviving columns finite) and Tier-2 GPU (sanity sweep golden ± range ~61 evals; adversarial poses ±200 mm off-axis, behind camera, 90°/180° rotations; assert finite AND cudaGetLastError() == cudaSuccess after each eval — the sticky-error trap at render_engine.cu:713; DIRECT_MAHFOUZ at an empty-silhouette pose EXPECT NaN today, green after the guard fix). Six failure modes code-grounded (degenerate projection, zero denominator, empty silhouette, uninitialized memory, fragment overflow = mute evals, int overflow ruled out). [Source: angles/02-cost-path-foundation.org, Round 2]
- Cross-angle consequence: GLh's trigger question (angle 01 Finding 3) is answered — the trigger exists but only outside the oracle's cost, so GLh is conditional on the three emitters, and the finite-check is justified on its own (a latent bug class), independent of GLh. [Source: angles/01-direct-variants.org R2-4; angles/02-cost-path-foundation.org, Round 2]

** Finding 9 — (Round 2) gb phase-switch: the numbers are canonical (5 / every-5th, Gb-DISIMPL), but the DIRECTGO reference code inverts the phases relative to the paper and every sibling port
- Canonical semantics, verified in three independent DIRECTGO artifacts plus the paper prose (Mathematics 2022 §2.4.5): during stagnation (fMinNotImpr > 5, non-security iteration) selection is restricted to the global phase (largest ~25% of size groups); on improvement and on security iterations (every 5th stagnant iteration, mod 5 == 0) the full two-phase selection runs; Yaro_epsilon 0.01 counts consecutive non-improving iterations (|Δf_min| < 1% relative). The "recommended values [10,28]" in the paper are bibliography references — [10] = Gb-BIRECT (ESWA 144:113052, 2020; its own port uses 2n/every-10th), [28] = Gb-DISIMPL (JOG 59:545–567, 2014; threshold 5/every-5th — the numbers 1-DTC-GL-gb uses). [Source: angles/01-direct-variants.org, R2-1]
- The contradiction: DIRECTGO's I_DTC_GL.m Selection 'gb' branch reads `if (fMinNotImpr > 5) && (mod(fMinNotImpr,5) ~= 0) → local distance-based set; else → global-only` — the exact inverse of the paper prose and of sDISIMPLvGlob.m / sGb_BIRECT.m / GENDIRECT/Refinement.m. Round 1's prose described the canonical semantics correctly but quoted the literal (inverted) code branch. Which semantics produced the paper's Table 2 numbers (0.7840 success) is unverifiable (the repo file's state at experiment time is unknown). [Source: angles/01-direct-variants.org, R2-1]
- JTML action: implement the CANONICAL semantics (two-phase while improving + security iterations; global-only beyond 5 stagnant iterations; Yaro_epsilon 0.01) and run a second ablation arm replicating the code-as-shipped inversion; the battery includes a gb-semantics pin (two-phase/global-only iteration trace on a stalled quadratic) so the harness knows which variant it measured; a replication subset (1-DTC-GL-gb vs 1-DTC-GL on the n=2/5 v1.2 subset at large budgets) can determine empirically which semantics reproduces the paper's reported ordering. [Source: angles/01-direct-variants.org, R2-1]

** Finding 10 — (Round 2) The split tie-break divergence is quantified: the repo splits Z where the studied 1-DTC splits X on the first branch/leaf split — a faithful 1-DTC-GL-gb landing requires the least-split rule
- Study's 1-DTC rule (verbatim, arXiv:2109.14912 §2.3.1): trisect the single longest side; ties break to the coordinate split the fewest times so far (global counter, unit space), then lowest index. DIRECTGO I_DTC_GL.m implements exactly this (min per-dimension LL, minas global counter, first-match). Repo rule: largest side in PHYSICAL units via DenormalizeRange(...).GetLargestDirection() with first-match lowest-index tie-break (direct_optimizer.cpp:159; data_structures_6D.cpp) — no global split counter. [Source: angles/01-direct-variants.org, R2-2]
- Divergence arithmetic against the actual stage ranges (settings_constants.h): trunk (35×6) — first split matches; branch (15,15,25,25,25,25) — denormalized (30,30,50,50,50,50) → repo picks Z, study picks X (all LL equal, lowest index); leaf (3,3,15,3,3,3) — denormalized (6,6,30,6,6,6) → repo picks Z, study picks X. "The repo is 1-DTC-alike" is exactly true only on the trunk; branch/leaf refine in the opposite dimension order from the studied 1-DTC. [Source: angles/01-direct-variants.org, R2-2]
- Consequence: the landing variant 1-DTC-GL-gb (as studied) uses the least-split rule, so a faithful port requires changing the split rule — a real behavior change to be scored by the battery, not a no-op. Battery probes to distinguish the rules: (i) a Tier-0 reference pin of the least-split dimension-selection sequence vs the repo's (assert the per-iteration split-dimension traces differ); (ii) the anisotropic-range probe (run the analytic cost with the actual branch/leaf ranges as box bounds — the first-split Z-vs-X divergence is deterministic and observable); (iii) DIRECTGOLib problems with per-dimension bounds (perturbed domains from Mathematics 2022 Table A2) where denormalized side ∝ bound width re-introduces the divergence. [Source: angles/01-direct-variants.org, R2-2]

* Contradictions and Open Questions

** Contradiction 1 — Dilation schedule: 6/3/1 (docs) vs 6/4/1 (code) — RE-STATED (Round 2: still open numerically; arbitration instrument now exists)
- Angle 02 resolved this with source evidence: the code implements 6/4/1 — settings_control.cpp:1201–1206 sets branch=4, leaf=1; settings_constants.h TRUNK_DILATION=6 / BRANCH_DILATION_DECREASE=2 / Z_SEARCH_DILATION=1 agree (consumed only by the experimental SettingsBridge); production OptimizerManager reads the per-manager "Dilation" runtime parameter. The 6/3/1 claim lives only in golden_oracle.org prose + baseline.json. Both agree on trunk 6 and leaf 1; the conflict is branch only (4 vs 3). Neither was ever runtime-captured (the flat-3000 oracle never exercises branch/leaf). Evidence favors 6/4/1 as implemented intent; docs are the stale artifact. Round 2 adds the arbitration vehicle: the z-profile probe sweeps at dilations {6,3,1,4} and the ablation manifest treats the schedule as data, so the contradiction becomes a measured choice rather than a docs dispute. Resolution path: Tier-0 registry/constants pins → z-profile/ablation data → update golden_oracle.org + baseline.json to the measured value or change settings_control.cpp:1204. [Source: angles/02-cost-path-foundation.org, "Dilation 6/4/1 vs 6/3/1"; angles/03-measurement-apparatus.org, R2-2; angles/04-backend-architecture.org, "What Could Not Be Verified"]

** Contradiction 2 — Variant recommendations (angle 01) vs the z-axis (angles 03/06) — RESOLVED (Round 2) as orthogonal mechanisms with a harness contract
- Angle 01 R2-6 resolved this head-on: the z-sensitivity ranking is a property of the COST FUNCTION at a fixed pose (observability); the DIRECT variant is a property of the SEARCH SCHEME (which poses get sampled). A variant cannot change what a fixed cost observes, and no selection scheme can "find" a z the cost does not see. Two documented second-order interactions: (i) the NaN/Inf trigger (GLh changes which poses are effectively searched when a cost fails on some poses); (ii) refinement control on z-flat costs (gb/rev's local-phase suppression is a pure-efficiency win; GL's unconditional local phase wastes evals). Harness contract: fix the cost family and sweep variants recording BOTH evals-to-target (search efficiency) and the recovered z-error distribution (observability) — a variant-switch win must never be read as a z fix; report z-error separately from evals in ablation.json. [Source: angles/01-direct-variants.org, R2-6; angles/03-measurement-apparatus.org, R2-2]

** Contradiction 3 — Perf cuts vs determinism: the docs' "atomics aren't bit-reproducible" claim vs the verified int-atomic cost path — RE-STATED (reaffirmed by Round 2)
- Angle 05 verified every active cost-path reduction is an int atomicAdd/atomicSub (fast_implant_dilation_metric.cu:145,147; distance_map_metric.cu:46–47; gpu_metrics.cu:129; iou.cu:66–72) — integer addition is order-independent, so results ARE bit-reproducible given identical launch configs and inputs. The order-nondeterministic float atomicAdd lives in the DRR fill (render_drr_engine.cu), which is NOT in the DIRECT cost path. Resolution: the docs' claim is stale; the determinism twin is a pose→score diff harness plus the ablation runner's rerun_identical check; every perf cut (async copies, batching) is gated on the diff being empty. The one cut with a real determinism caveat is Cut 3 (fragment-fill kernel change), which must preserve per-thread work for threads < fragment_fill exactly. ## Round 2

### Summary

Round 1's structural claims are now converted into measured, ordered cut recipes with exact file:line placements, pre-registered predictions, and per-cut gates. New source-verified findings this round: (1) the clock() meter is not just CPU-only — it carries a 1000× unit error on Linux (glibc clock() returns microseconds; the code labels the raw ticks "ms/call" with no CLOCKS_PER_SEC division anywhere in src/, and the UI's "Iterations Per Second" at mainscreen.cpp:4654-4655 divides 1000.0 by the raw µs value → ~1000× understated, with the ETA math at :4598/:4659 off by the same factor); (2) there are TWO meter sites (optimizer_manager.cpp:1197-1203 end-of-frame, :1272-1279 iteration callback — the dispatch's :1274-1281 is the latter), and the QML/experimental UI relays no speed at all (OptimizerBridge.h has no speed property; the widgets-path MainScreen::onUpdateDisplay at view/mainscreen.cpp:4582 is the only consumer); (3) Cut 3's fixed grid is bounded by arithmetic: dev_stride_prefixes_ (maximum_stride_size = 10M ints) caps the fragment fill at ~2.55e9 via the existing host guard (render_engine.cu:795-800), and both fill kernels already guard their ENTIRE body — including FillTriangleKernel's shared-memory load and __syncthreads (:636-641) — behind `i < total` (:628-629), so a fixed grid larger than the true count is bit-safe with NO kernel-source change; the open questions are the measured fragment distribution and the empty-grid launch cost; (4) eval-state ownership for Cut 2 is pinned to the code: RenderEngine owns renderer_output_ (a GPUImage: dev_image_ cudaMalloc + pinned bounding_box_, gpu_image.cu:13-40), GPUMetrics owns the score buffers (gpu_metrics.cu:7-65), OptimizerManager constructs GPUMetrics at :818 — so "compute owns buffer state, manager owns graph" (angle 04 R2-4) maps to a second renderer_output_ inside RenderEngine + a second score-buffer bank inside GPUMetrics, with no manager-graph change. Cut order is unchanged (0 instrument → 1 async terminal copies → 2 iteration batching → 3 conditional fragment-fill removal → 4 meter fix) but each cut now has an executable spec, a prediction sourced from Cut 0's data, and a revert rule.

### Key Findings (Round 2)

#### R2-1 — The clock() meter has a 1000× unit error on Linux, on top of the CPU-time blind spot

- grep of src/ for CLOCKS_PER_SEC: zero hits — the meter divides raw clock() ticks by calls with no unit conversion: `static_cast<double>(clock() - start_clock_) / static_cast<double>(cost_function_calls_)` (optimizer_manager.cpp:1198-1199) and the RunDirectStage twin (:1274-1275).
- On Linux glibc, clock() returns microseconds (CLOCKS_PER_SEC = 1e6; MSVC uses 1000). The code labels the value "ms/call"; the actual value is CPU-µs/call → 1000× unit error. The JTA codebase is a Windows-Qt origin, so this is plausibly port-induced — but on this Linux/pixi build the error is live.
- UI consumption compounds it: "Iterations Per Second: 1000.0 / iteration_speed" (view/mainscreen.cpp:4654-4655) with iteration_speed in µs/call yields calls-per-ms — 1000× understated (and further understated because CPU time excludes sync-wait). The ETA `(budget − calls) / (1000.0 / iteration_speed)` (:4598, :4659) produces remaining milliseconds displayed as mm:ss — ~1000× overstated.
- Severity: medium-high for the meter's purpose (user-facing speed/ETA are wrong by ~3 orders of magnitude; no before/after perf claim through this meter is meaningful); high as a correctness fact.
- Confidence: high (code path verified; no CLOCKS_PER_SEC anywhere; the platform unit semantics are POSIX-standard). The "port-induced" attribution is medium (original codebase not verifiable here).
- Relevance: Cut 4 must (a) switch to steady_clock wall time and (b) emit TRUE ms/call so the existing UI math (1000.0/ms_per_call) becomes correct without a UI-side change.

#### R2-2 — Two meter sites, one UI consumer, and a QML gap

- Site 1: end-of-frame emit, optimizer_manager.cpp:1197-1203 (uses cost_function_calls_, the running frame-level counter).
- Site 2: RunDirectStage iteration-callback emit, optimizer_manager.cpp:1272-1279 (uses opt.GetCostFunctionCalls()) — the dispatch's :1274-1281. Both must be replaced by Cut 4.
- Relay chain (verified): UpdateDisplay(double,int,double,unsigned int) → OptimizerRunController::onManagerUpdateDisplay (coordinator/optimizer_run_controller.cpp:243) → updateDisplayRelayed → MainScreen::onUpdateDisplay (view/mainscreen.cpp:4582) — the ONLY reader; renders the VTK actor text (speed, calls, level, ETA).
- QML/experimental path: OptimizerBridge.h exposes stageText/costCalls but NO speed property (grep-verified zero matches) — the QML UI never displays ms/call. If the user wants the meter in the experimental UI, one bridge property is a small additive change (flagged out of Cut 4's scope).
- Severity: low-medium (defines Cut 4's surface; the widgets path is the production meter today).
- Confidence: high (signal chain grep-verified end to end).

#### R2-3 — Cut 3's fixed grid is bounded by arithmetic: stride-prefix capacity + in-kernel guards make it a host-side change

- dev_stride_prefixes_ is allocated once at maximum_stride_size × sizeof(int) = 10M × 4 B = 40 MB (render_engine.cu InitializeCUDA, :311-312 region). StridePrefixKernel writes one entry per 256-fragment stride group (index i, guarded i < total/256, :592-593); FillTriangleKernel reads dev_stride_prefixes[blockIdx.x] with blockIdx.x < total/256. Both stay in-bounds iff total ≤ maximum_stride_size × 256 ≈ 2.56e9.
- The existing host overflow guard is `fragment_fill_[0] > maximum_stride_size × (threads_per_block − 1)` = 2.55e9 (render_engine.cu:795-800), i.e., exactly the capacity bound (threads_per_block = 256, include/compute/cuda_launch_parameters.h). SAFE_CAP = maximum_stride_size × threads_per_block is the device-capacity ceiling; nothing above it is launchable anyway.
- Bit-safety of a fixed grid: BOTH fill kernels wrap their entire body — including FillTriangleKernel's shared-memory load and __syncthreads (:636-641) — inside `if (i < total)` (:628-629); StridePrefixKernel likewise (:592-593). Threads/blocks beyond the true count execute nothing and write nothing. Therefore launching grids computed from min(fragment_fill, GRID_CAP) needs NO kernel-source change: threads < total do exactly today's work.
- The real tractability question is launch cost, not correctness: a grid at the analytic ceiling is ceil(2.55e9/256) ≈ 10M blocks of FillTriangleKernel — schedulable (gridDim.x limit 2³¹−1) but with per-block overhead that must be measured. The worst-case analytic fragment count (all 12,412 facets spanning the full 1024² image ≈ 1.3e10) exceeds capacity, so overflow is geometrically possible in the extreme → the sync-fallback is mandatory, not optional.
- Severity: high (this arithmetic is what makes Cut 3's decision procedure executable — it shrinks the cut from "kernel-level change" to a host-side grid computation + measured GRID_CAP).
- Confidence: high (all guard/alloc lines verified).

#### R2-4 — Cut 2's double-buffer ownership is pinned to the code (compute owns state; manager owns graph)

- Today: RenderEngine owns renderer_output_ per camera — a GPUImage whose dev_image_ (cudaMalloc) and bounding_box_ (pinned cudaHostAlloc) are allocated in the GPUImage ctor (gpu_image.cu:13-40) and freed in the dtor; renderer_output_ is created in RenderEngine::InitializeCUDA (render_engine.cu:319). GPUMetrics owns the score buffers: pinned host pixel_score_/distance_map_score_/edge_pixels_count_ + device dev_pixel_score_/dev_distance_map_score_/dev_edge_pixels_count_, all in the ctor (gpu_metrics.cu:7-65), freed in the dtor (:68-95). OptimizerManager constructs GPUMetrics once in Initialize (optimizer_manager.cpp:818) and hands it by pointer to all three CFMs (CostFunctionManager.cpp:122).
- Target (per angle 04 R2-4): compute owns buffer STATE → (a) a second render output inside RenderEngine (renderer_output_b_, same width/height/device, allocated next to :319); (b) a second bank INSIDE GPUMetrics — dev_pixel_score_[2], dev_distance_map_score_[2], dev_edge_pixels_count_[2] plus pinned twins, with SetActiveBank(int) toggling. One object with doubled internal state keeps the manager's graph (one GPUMetrics, three CFMs by pointer) untouched. The alternation logic lives in the cost layer (the batched adapter in compute).
- The eval path still allocates nothing per call (buffers exist at init; cudaMemcpyAsync into the pinned banks).
- Severity: high (the buffer/allocation answer the dispatch asked for).
- Confidence: high (ownership verified in gpu_image.cu / gpu_metrics.cu / optimizer_manager.cpp:818 / CostFunctionManager.cpp:122).

#### R2-5 — Round-1 line-span correction + the instrumentation layer constraint

- costFunctionDIRECT_DILATION spans DIRECT_DILATION.cpp:58-107 (round 1 cited :67-106; the signature is at :58). Composition order verified: RenderPrimaryCamera → FastImplantDilationMetric → DistanceMapMetric (monoplane), biplane branch at :88-105.
- nvtx3 must NOT enter jtml_domain: DirectOptimizer is the "zero Qt/VTK/CUDA" extraction (direct_optimizer.h:11-13) — the per-iteration range therefore lives in the coordinator's iteration callback (optimizer_manager.cpp:1263-1280), which fires exactly once per ConvexHull+Trisect iteration (direct_optimizer.cpp:41-49), NOT inside DirectOptimizer. All per-eval/per-stage ranges live in compute (jtml_compute, where the toolkit include path already applies).
- Severity: medium (a layer-purity constraint that shapes every instrumentation placement).
- Confidence: high (header contract + callback wiring verified).

### The instrumentation protocol (Cut 0) — the first deliverable

Goal: replace the derived 20-60 evals/s estimate with a measured per-eval record and make the item-8 claim (sync-bound, not kernel-bound) arbitrable by data. Behavior change: none. Compile-in always (nvtx3 is header-only, ~ns per range when idle).

### Cut 1 — async terminal copies + one event wait per eval (full spec)

The 3 terminal copies (of the 5) become cudaMemcpyAsync into the EXISTING pinned buffers; the 2 render syncs (bounding-box render_engine.cu:781-785, fragment :786-790) STAY synchronous — the host needs the bbox to size the metric launch grids (fast_implant_dilation_metric.cu:201-207, distance_map_metric.cu:83-89) and the fragment count to size the fill launches (render_engine.cu:812-816, :823-826). - fast_implant_dilation_metric.cu:289-290 (pixel_score_ ← dev_pixel_score_) → cudaMemcpyAsync
- distance_map_metric.cu:110-114 (distance_map_score_ ← dev_distance_map_score_) → cudaMemcpyAsync
- distance_map_metric.cu:115-119 (edge_pixels_count_ ← dev_edge_pixels_count_) → cudaMemcpyAsync

Bit-identity argument (Cut 1): cudaMemcpyAsync on the same default stream does not reorder kernels or copies — the device-side execution sequence is byte-for-byte today's; only the host's blocking pattern changes. All reductions are int atomicAdd/atomicSub (fast_implant_dilation_metric.cu:145,147; distance_map_metric.cu:46-47) — commutative and associative, value-deterministic given identical launch configs and inputs; launch configs depend only on the bbox, which is unchanged. The pinned buffers contain identical values at event completion; the host assembly reads the same values in the same order ⇒ bit-identical scores. Gate: pose→score diff empty.

Also in Cut 1: delete the stray `cudaGetLastError(); // Resets Errors (MAYBE DELETE TO SAVE TIME?)` at render_engine.cu:713 — Render() already returns cudaGetLastError() at :839, so the reset is redundant; removing it drops one per-eval host-driver round trip. Behavior-neutral for errors (the tail check still surfaces sticky errors). Coordinate landing order with angle 02's adversarial GPU probe (which asserts cudaGetLastError() == cudaSuccess per eval): the deletion does not change sticky-error semantics, so the probe's expectation is unchanged.

Biplane freebie (fold into Cut 1): with the primary metrics' copies async, the secondary Render + FastImplantDilationMetric (separate camera buffers, gpu_model.cu:26-35) enqueue behind them on the same stream; one event wait at the end of the biplane branch (DIRECT_DILATION.cpp:88-105). No double-buffering needed.

First capture on a reduced budget (a small dedicated run — the oracle's kBudget=3000 is "few minutes", oracle_test.cpp:244), then one full 3-frame run. ncu for kernel-level data (already in the env):

```sh
ncu --set basic --kernel-name 'regex:FillTriangleKernel|FastImplantDilationMetric_DilateKernel|DistanceMapMetric_Kernel' .build/bin/jtml_test_oracle
```

(ncu needs profiling permissions on the box; kernel-level metrics are the sanity check that no hidden fat kernel exists.)

The exact first-run record (replaces the derived 20-60 evals/s estimate):

1. Per-eval event time: mean / p50 / p95 over frame-0's 3000 evals, plus per-eval wall time alongside.
2. Stage split: render total, fast-implant total, distance-map total (event deltas) — the "which stage owns the time" answer.
3. Kernel breakdown: the ~15 launches' individual times (nsys kern_sum: ResetKernel, WorldToPixelKernel, BoundingBoxForTrianglesKernel, BoundingBoxSizesKernel, cub ExclusiveSum, PrepareLaunchPacketKernel, StridePrefixKernel, FillTriangleKernel, fast-implant reset/edge/dilate/difference, distance-map resets + main kernel).
4. D2H stalls: per-sync duration + host-block gap for each of the 5 copies (nsys mem_time_sum + the nvtx sync marks) — the load-bearing numbers: which of the ~3 host-block windows dominates.
5. Gaps: idle intervals between kernel spans (launch latency, host crop math at fast_implant_dilation_metric.cu:201-207 / distance_map_metric.cu:83-89, overflow check at render_engine.cu:795-808).
6. Totals: evals/s = 3000/wall; GPU-active% = Σkernels/wall; sync-stall% = ΣD2H stalls/wall; the item-8 verdict = sync-stall% vs kernel%.
7. Meter gap: clock()-meter value (both sites) vs event ms/call vs wall ms/call — recorded, with the R2-1 unit error quantified.
8. Fragment sweep (feeds Cut 3's trigger): fragment_fill_[0] min/max/p99/max-ever + bbox crop sizes per eval over the same 3000 evals (the values are already on the host at render_engine.cu:786-790).

The record is saved as a run artifact (perf.json or a section in baseline.json's sibling); it is the pre-registration source for Cuts 1-3's predicted Δ.

### Cut 1 — async terminal copies + one event wait per eval (full spec)

The 3 terminal copies (of the 5) become cudaMemcpyAsync into the EXISTING pinned buffers; the 2 render syncs (bounding-box render_engine.cu:781-785, fragment :786-790) STAY synchronous — the host needs the bbox to size the metric launch grids (fast_implant_dilation_metric.cu:201-207, distance_map_metric.cu:83-89) and the fragment count to size the fill launches (render_engine.cu:812-816, :823-826). These are data-dependent launch configs; removing them requires moving the crop math onto the device (out of scope; interacts with angle 02's metric semantics).

Conversions:

- fast_implant_dilation_metric.cu:289-290 (pixel_score_ ← dev_pixel_score_) → cudaMemcpyAsync
- distance_map_metric.cu:110-114 (distance_map_score_ ← dev_distance_map_score_) → cudaMemcpyAsync
- distance_map_metric.cu:115-119 (edge_pixels_count_ ← dev_edge_pixels_count_) → cudaMemcpyAsync

All targets are pinned (GPUMetrics ctor, gpu_metrics.cu:7-65) — zero allocation work.

The one event wait: costFunctionDIRECT_DILATION (DIRECT_DILATION.cpp:58-107) is restructured into enqueue → cudaEventRecord → cudaEventSynchronize → assemble. The two metric functions issue their async copies and return WITHOUT reading the pinned values; the cost callback records the event after the last enqueue, waits once, then reads pixel_score_, distance_map_score_, edge_pixels_count_ and assembles `white_sum + (−1·pixel_score) + dm_score/(edge_count+0.1)` in exactly today's order (the +0.1 guard and all int math untouched). Net effect: 3 sync round-trips → 1 event wait; the distance-map pair's two syncs and the pixel-score sync merge into one drain; the copies overlap the kernels' tails on the default stream.

Bit-identity argument (Cut 1): cudaMemcpyAsync on the same default stream does not reorder kernels or copies — the device-side execution sequence is byte-for-byte today's; only the host's blocking pattern changes. All reductions are int atomicAdd/atomicSub (fast_implant_dilation_metric.cu:145,147; distance_map_metric.cu:46-47) — commutative and associative, value-deterministic given identical launch configs and inputs; launch configs depend only on the bbox, which is unchanged. The pinned buffers contain identical values at event completion; the host assembly reads the same values in the same order ⇒ bit-identical scores. Gate: pose→score diff empty.

Also in Cut 1: delete the stray `cudaGetLastError(); // Resets Errors (MAYBE DELETE TO SAVE TIME?)` at render_engine.cu:713 — Render() already returns cudaGetLastError() at :839, so the reset is redundant; removing it drops one per-eval host-driver round trip. Behavior-neutral for errors (the tail check still surfaces sticky errors). Coordinate landing order with angle 02's adversarial GPU probe (which asserts cudaGetLastError() == cudaSuccess per eval): the deletion does not change sticky-error semantics, so the probe's expectation is unchanged.

Biplane freebie (fold into Cut 1): with the primary metrics' copies async, the secondary Render + FastImplantDilationMetric (separate camera buffers, gpu_model.cu:26-35) enqueue behind them on the same stream; one event wait at the end of the biplane branch (DIRECT_DILATION.cpp:88-105). No double-buffering needed.

Prediction (pre-registered after Cut 0): Δ = measured sync-stall sum of the 3 converted copies + 2-3 driver round-trips − one event wait ≈ the merge of drains #2+#3 (fast-implant + distance-map). If Cut 0 shows those drains are small (< 5% of wall), the cut still lands (pure win) but the emphasis moves to Cut 2. Gate: headless green, oracle green, bit-identity empty, mean per-eval event-time reduction ≥ prediction.

### Cut 2 — iteration batching + double-buffered eval state (full spec)

Domain seam (per angle 04 R2-4 clause 1): DirectOptimizer gains ONE optional sibling of the same type family — `using BatchCostFunction = std::function<std::vector<double>(const std::vector<Point6D>&)>` + SetBatchCostFunction (no CUDA types in direct_optimizer.h; the :11-13 "zero Qt/VTK/CUDA" contract intact). In TrisectPotentiallyOptimal, collect the iteration's changed-center poses in exactly the sequential order (box i in potentially_optimal_hyperboxes_ order; A then B per box — direct_optimizer.cpp:158-178 region), call the batch callback once, then replay per pose in order: cost_function_calls_++ (EvaluateCostFunction's bookkeeping), best-value update + improvement callback, AddHyperBox. Identical stored values, identical optimum, identical callback order (contract clause 2). The seed eval (Run(), direct_optimizer.cpp:38) stays sequential. No batch surface set ⇒ today's loop, byte-for-byte.

Buffers and allocation (which buffers, who allocates — "compute owns state, manager owns graph"):

- Render output: a second GPUImage inside RenderEngine (renderer_output_b_, same width/height/device), constructed in InitializeCUDA next to renderer_output_ (render_engine.cu:319); dev_image_ (cudaMalloc) + pinned bounding_box_ (cudaHostAlloc) come from the GPUImage ctor (gpu_image.cu:13-40).
- Score buffers: a second bank INSIDE GPUMetrics — dev_pixel_score_[2], dev_distance_map_score_[2], dev_edge_pixels_count_[2] plus pinned twins pixel_score_[2]/distance_map_score_[2]/edge_pixels_count_[2], allocated in the ctor (gpu_metrics.cu:7-65), freed in the dtor (:68-95), with SetActiveBank(int). ONE GPUMetrics object with doubled internal state — the manager's graph (constructed at optimizer_manager.cpp:818, passed by pointer to the 3 CFMs, CostFunctionManager.cpp:122) is unchanged. The alternation logic lives in the cost layer (the batched adapter in compute).
- The in-place mutation constraint (round 1) is exactly why two banks: FastImplantDilationMetric writes EDGE/DILATED into the render output (fast_implant_dilation_metric.cu:218-271) and DistanceMapMetric reads that same buffer (:46-50) — eval k on bank k%2 cannot collide with eval k+1 on bank (k+1)%2.

Enqueue-before-wait seam (contract clause 4): the batched callback loops poses k=0..N−1: bank = k%2; SetPose + Render into bank (the bbox/fragment sync at render_engine.cu:781-790 STILL blocks the host per eval — that is the point: eval k's host-block overlaps eval k−1's already-enqueued metric kernels on the GPU); run the metrics into bank; enqueue the 3 async terminal copies into bank's pinned scores; cudaEventRecord(ev[k]). After the loop: cudaEventSynchronize on the last event (or all events), read all scores in input order, return the vector. The mid-eval fragment sync stays inside compute. The per-eval event wait (Cut 1) is replaced by the per-iteration wait.

Headless-verifiable determinism argument: the replay contract is pure domain logic and testable without a GPU — a Tier-0 test (test/unit/test_direct_optimizer family) with a scripted batch cost asserts: (a) the batch callback receives exactly the pose sequence the sequential path evaluates (recorded from a sequential reference run on the same seed), (b) after Run(), the storage (DirectDataStorage columns/values), optimum location/value, GetCostFunctionCalls(), and the improvement/iteration callback sequences are identical between the sequential and batched paths fed the same scripted values. GPU-side bit-identity: identical kernels, launch configs, and stream order per eval; only host-wait interleaving changes; int-atomics ⇒ same scores. Verified by the pose→score diff harness on the oracle.

Prediction: after Cut 1, the per-eval host-block is the render drain + the terminal wait; batching hides both behind the previous eval's GPU work. Predicted Δ = the measured host-block-window sum from Cut 0 minus what Cut 1 already removed. Gate: headless green (incl. the new Tier-0 batch test), oracle green, bit-identity empty, per-eval event-time reduction ≥ prediction. Revert rule: if the batched path shows no improvement (or a regression) over 3 runs, abandon the jj change and keep sequential.

### Cut 3 — fragment-fill removal: the decision procedure (conditional)

Trigger measurement (during Cut 0): the fragment sweep (fragment_fill_[0] min/max/p99/max-ever + bbox per eval over frame-0's 3000 evals) plus the render-drain time (event gap from PrepareLaunchPacketKernel completion to the fill kernels' start).

Trigger condition (BOTH must hold; pre-registered from Cut 0's data):

(a) the render drain (bbox+fragment sync + overflow check + launch latency) is the dominant remaining per-eval stall after Cuts 1-2 — e.g., ≥ 50% of per-eval wall (number fixed from Cut 0's table);
(b) the fragment distribution is tightly bounded: max_observed × margin < SAFE_CAP = maximum_stride_size × threads_per_block = 2.55e9 (the capacity ceiling, R2-3), AND a GRID_CAP/256-block launch is affordable (measure the empty-grid launch time for the chosen GRID_CAP — the analytic ceiling would be ~10M blocks, so the practical GRID_CAP comes from the measured distribution, e.g., next power-of-two ≥ max_observed × 2).

Device-side clamp design (R2-3 makes it a host-side change): compute `fill = min(fragment_fill_[0], GRID_CAP)`; launch StridePrefixKernel and FillTriangleKernel from `fill` (ceil(fill/(256×256)) and ceil(fill/256) — the existing launch expressions at render_engine.cu:812-816/:823-826 with the value substituted). Optionally clamp on-device (PrepareLaunchPacketKernel writes min(fragment_fill, GRID_CAP) to a second device int) so the host never needs the true value to launch. NO kernel-source change: threads/blocks beyond the true total exit at the existing in-kernel guards (StridePrefixKernel :592-593; FillTriangleKernel :628-629, which wraps the whole body including the shared-mem load + __syncthreads :636-641), writing nothing. Non-overflow renders are bit-identical by construction (threads < total do exactly today's work).

Overflow semantics preserved (non-negotiable): if fragment_fill_[0] > GRID_CAP, the eval must NOT silently under-render (fragments in (GRID_CAP, total) would never be processed). Two safe behaviors: (i) per-eval fallback to the synchronous read + dynamic grid (the current path — keep the sync as the tail handler), or (ii) abort the frame exactly as today (fragment_overflow_ = true + cudaErrorMemoryAllocation, render_engine.cu:795-808). The fallback keeps bit-identity for all non-fallback evals and preserves error behavior for the tail. The bbox sync (:781-785) is NOT touched by Cut 3 (the crop/grid host math still needs it).

Safe fallback (the decision's default): if (a) or (b) fails — unbounded tail, or GRID_CAP blocks unaffordable — keep the fragment sync and accept it as the one structural cost; in the batched pipeline (Cut 2) its wait already overlaps the previous eval's tail, so the remaining exposure is small. This is a measured no-go, not a punt.

Prediction: Δ = the measured render-drain sum minus the residual fallback cost. Gate: oracle green, non-overflow bit-identity empty, overflow frames still error, event-time reduction ≥ prediction.

### Cut 4 — the event-based ms/call meter (full spec)

Replace BOTH clock() meters: optimizer_manager.cpp:1272-1279 (RunDirectStage iteration callback — the dispatch's :1274-1281) and :1197-1203 (end-of-frame emit). Both currently compute CPU-ticks/call (µs on Linux) and emit it as "ms/call" — CPU-only, GPU-blind, sync-blind, and 1000× unit-wrong (R2-1).

New meter spec:

- wall ms/call = std::chrono::steady_clock elapsed over the stage (RunDirectStage entry → current iteration callback) / opt.GetCostFunctionCalls() — wall INCLUDES GPU time and sync-wait time (the host blocks inside the driver), satisfying "includes GPU time".
- GPU ms/call = the cudaEvent per-eval deltas from Cut 0's instrumentation, accumulated per stage — logged alongside (or the meter owns one minimal event pair per stage if instrumentation is compiled out). wall − GPU = host overhead + sync stalls, reported so the item-8 claim stays visible in the UI's data trail.
- Units: emit TRUE ms/call. The existing UI math then becomes correct without UI changes: "Iterations Per Second: 1000.0 / iteration_speed" (view/mainscreen.cpp:4654-4655) and the ETA (:4598/:4659) both assume ms/call. The fix is at the meter, not the UI.
- Where the UI reads it (verified): UpdateDisplay(double iteration_speed, ...) → OptimizerRunController::onManagerUpdateDisplay (coordinator/optimizer_run_controller.cpp:243) → updateDisplayRelayed → MainScreen::onUpdateDisplay (view/mainscreen.cpp:4582; speed :4654-4655, ETA :4598/:4659, VTK actor text). The QML/experimental path (OptimizerBridge.h) relays no speed today (R2-2) — adding it is a separate small change if the QML UI needs the meter.
- No behavior change to the search. Gate: meter tracks the event-measured per-eval time within noise (wall ≥ event always; the gap is reported, not asserted).

### The measurement protocol every cut must pass

For Cuts 1-3 (Cut 4 is meter-only; Cut 0 is record-only):

(a) headless green — pixi run test (ctest -L headless, --timeout 600; the batch cut adds its Tier-0 replay test to this set);
(b) oracle green — ctest --test-dir .build -L oracle → jtml.oracle: IoU > 0.85 per frame (oracle_test.cpp:333; kIouGate :245, kBudget 3000 :244, TIMEOUT 3600 at test/CMakeLists.txt:1253). Runs only after the synthesis step-1 re-baseline so the gate compares against the trustworthy baseline;
(c) bit-identity diff empty — the pose→score recorder harness: the first 1000 evals of oracle frame 0 recorded as (pose, cost) pairs (recorder at the oracle cost lambda, oracle_test.cpp:288-291); diff vs the baseline recording after each cut. Empty where the cut claims bit-identity (Cuts 1, 2; Cut 3 on non-overflow evals);
(d) measured improvement ≥ prediction — each cut pre-registers its predicted Δ from Cut 0's table (Cut 1: converted-sync stall sum; Cut 2: host-block window sum; Cut 3: render-drain sum); acceptance = mean per-eval event-time reduction over the same 3000-eval sequence ≥ prediction, reproducible over 3 runs.

Revert rule: a cut that measures < prediction (or a regression) is reverted in the same jj change (jj abandon) with the measurement recorded in the run's artifacts; the cut may be retried only with a new prediction derived from the new baseline. Cuts land in order 0 → 1 → 2 → 4 → (3 conditional) — Cut 3 never before Cut 2, Cut 4 before any cut is demonstrated to the user via the UI.

### What Could Not Be Verified (Round 2)

- The actual fragment_fill_ distribution and render-drain times — need the GPU sweep on the RTX 3090 (Cut 0, record item 8). Cut 3's go/no-go is unmeasured until then.
- Whether nvtx3 resolves in the coordinator TUs (include-path question — verify at build; the additive toolkit-include fallback is specified).
- The empty-grid launch cost of a large fixed GRID_CAP (measure at Cut 3 trigger time; the analytic ceiling of ~10M blocks is schedulable but plausibly ms-scale).
- Whether cudaEventSynchronize per eval (Cut 1) still pays a meaningful driver wake-up on this driver/arch — the measurement decides whether Cut 2's restructuring is justified.
- The user-visible magnitude of the R2-1 unit bug (the code path is verified; the numbers on the user's display were not captured).
- GPUMetrics' SetActiveBank semantics vs the three per-stage CFMs sharing one instance (the stage loop is sequential so no interleave by construction, but the invariant is asserted, not yet tested).

**Deliverable:** Appended a `## Round 2` section to `angles/05-compute-perf.org` converting round 1's structural claims into measured, ordered cut recipes — every claim re-verified against source at exact file:line before writing.

**What was verified fresh this round (source-reading, not round-1 reuse):**
- Zero `cudaEvent`/`cudaStreamCreate`/`cudaMemcpyAsync`/`nvtx` anywhere in `src/` (grep-confirmed) — Cut 1's "3 terminal copies → async" is a genuinely green-field change.

- **R2-4:** Cut 2's double-buffer ownership pinned: `RenderEngine::renderer_output_` (GPUImage ctor, `gpu_image.cu:13-40`), `GPUMetrics` score buffers (`gpu_metrics.cu:7-65`), manager constructs GPUMetrics at `:818` — matching angle 04's R2-4 contract (compute owns state, manager owns graph, one optional batch `std::function` sibling).

**Cut specs delivered (all in the appended section):** Cut 0 instrumentation protocol (nvtx3 placement table with file:line, cudaEvent placements, nsys/ncu recipes, 8-item first-run record replacing the 20-60 evals/s estimate); Cut 1 (3 async terminal copies, one event wait, bit-identity argument, `:713` deletion, biplane freebie); Cut 2 (batch seam, buffer/allocator spec, enqueue-before-wait, headless Tier-0 determinism test); Cut 3 (two-condition trigger, clamp design, safe fallback); Cut 4 (steady_clock wall + cudaEvent GPU time, unit fix, UI read path); per-cut gate protocol (a–d) with the revert rule.
